reason_not_chosen.text: Hunt's "about 2" is a rounded report of the same arrival that Meade himself puts at 1 a.m.

weighing.summary: Meade states his own arrival (1 a.m.); Hunt, who relays it, says about 2; the plan's "after midnight" agrees; "about 04:00" has no source.
weighing.who: Meade commanded the army and wrote the passage about his own arrival; Hunt, chief of artillery, relays it; the 04:00 value comes from a web timeline.
weighing.when: Meade wrote on 1 Oct 1863 and Hunt on 27 Sep 1863: both are reports of the autumn, 3 months after the event, the best record there is.
weighing.where: Meade was the man who arrived; Hunt's place at the time is not stated in the passage.
weighing.how_knew: Meade knew from his own ride; Hunt's "about" marks a rounded hearsay figure.
weighing.clock: Both reports use the Union clock; no correction for the Confederate clock is needed.
weighing.independence: Meade and Hunt are two writers but Hunt may rely on Meade's headquarters; counted as one line of knowledge for the default.

source_panel_text: About 01:00 on Jul 2: Meade's own report puts his arrival at 1 a.m. and his inspection of the line at first light. Hunt's report says about 2 a.m. The plan's "after midnight" agrees; "about 04:00" (one web timeline) has no source in the record. All four values stay selectable.

pdf_default.note: The plan's 01:00 agrees with Meade; its word pre-dawn is first light in Meade.

first_delegated.note: The first delegated default is confirmed unchanged by the reading of the report.

what_would_change_it: A dated order or dispatch of 2 July placing the arrival of the commanding general at another hour.
